en: 9. Dhammayamaka 9.2 Pavattivāra 9.2.2.
Nirodhavāra (The Chapter on Cessation)
9.2.2.1. Chapter on the Present (Paccuppannavāra) 9.2.2.1.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) In whom wholesome states cease, in him unwholesome states cease? No.
Or again, for whom unwholesome states cease, for that person do wholesome states cease? No.
For whom wholesome states cease, for that person do indeterminate states cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states in the immaterial realm, for those persons wholesome states cease, but indeterminate states do not [cease].
Mental phenomena cease. At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states in the five-aggregate plane, both wholesome phenomena and indeterminate phenomena cease for them.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate phenomena cease, do wholesome phenomena cease for them?
For all those passing away, at the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence,
indeterminate states cease, but wholesome states do not cease for them. In the five-aggregate realm,
at the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, both indeterminate states and wholesome states cease for them.
For whom unwholesome states cease, for them indeterminate states cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states in the immaterial realm, unwholesome states cease for them, but indeterminate states do not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states in the five-aggregate realm, unwholesome states cease for them... [and so on].
And indeterminate states cease.
Or, in whomsoever indeterminate states cease, do unwholesome states cease in them?
In all those passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome during the course of existence, indeterminate states [cease].

Indeterminate states cease, but unwholesome states do not cease for them. At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states in the five-aggregate plane, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states cease for them.
9.2.2.1.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states cease, do unwholesome states cease there? Yes.
Or, wherever unwholesome states cease, do wholesome states cease there? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states cease, do indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or again: Wherever indeterminate states cease, do wholesome states cease there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states cease there, but wholesome states do not cease there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence, both indeterminate states and wholesome states cease there.
Wherever unwholesome states cease, do indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or, where indeterminate states cease, do unwholesome states cease there?

In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states cease there, but unwholesome states do not cease there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states cease there.
9.2.2.1.3. Positive Correlation: Person and Plane (Anulomapuggalokāsa)
When wholesome states cease for someone at a certain place, do unwholesome states cease for that person at that same place? No.
Or rather, when unwholesome states cease for someone at a certain place, do wholesome states cease for that person at that same place? No.
When wholesome states cease for someone at a certain place, do indeterminate states cease for that person at that same place?
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states in the immaterial realm, wholesome phenomena cease for those persons there,
but indeterminate phenomena do not cease for them there. At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states in the five-aggregate realm,
both wholesome phenomena and indeterminate phenomena cease for those persons there.
Or again, for whom and where indeterminate states cease, for them do wholesome states cease there?

For all those passing away, and for those during the course of existence at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome—therein indeterminate states cease, but wholesome states do not cease for them there. [In the case of] the fivefold plane, for those who are wholesome...
At the moment of dissolution, both indeterminate states and wholesome states cease therein.
For whomsoever unwholesome states cease therein, do indeterminate states cease for them therein?
At the moment of dissolution of unwholesome states in the immaterial realm, unwholesome states cease for them therein, but indeterminate states do not [cease] for them.
Therein, indeterminate states cease. In the five-aggregate plane, at the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, both unwholesome states and indeterminate states cease therein.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states cease therein, do unwholesome states also cease for them therein?
In all those passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome during the course of existence,
indeterminate states cease there, but unwholesome states do not cease there for them. In the five-aggregate realm,
at the moment of dissolution of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states cease there for them.
9.2.2.1.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states do not cease, for that person do unwholesome states not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, for those [persons] wholesome states do not cease, but unwholesome states do not [necessarily] cease for them.
They do not cease. For all [beings] at the moment of arising of consciousness,
for those at the moment of dissolution of consciousness dissociated from both the wholesome and the unwholesome, for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings,
neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states cease.
Or rather, for whom unwholesome states do not cease, for them wholesome states do not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, unwholesome states do not cease for them, but wholesome states do not fail to cease for them.
For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those whose consciousness is dissociated from the unwholesome and dissociated from the wholesome...
At the moment of dissolution, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings,
neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states cease.
For one in whom wholesome states do not cease, do indeterminate states also not cease?
For all those passing away, at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence,
wholesome states do not cease, yet indeterminate states do not fail to cease for them. For all those being reborn,
at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of dissolution of an unwholesome consciousness, both wholesome states...
Indeterminate states do not cease. Or, for whom indeterminate states do not cease, do wholesome states not cease for them?
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states in the formless realm, indeterminate states do not cease for them, yet wholesome states [do] not [cease] for them.

Indeterminate states do not cease. For all those being reborn, for those in the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those in the immaterial plane at the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states—indeterminate states do not cease and wholesome states also do not cease for them.
For whom unwholesome states do not cease, do indeterminate states not cease for them?
For all those passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from unwholesome states during the course of existence,
unwholesome phenomena do not cease, yet indeterminate phenomena do not fail to cease for them. For all those being reborn,
at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of dissolution of wholesome states in the formless realm, unwholesome phenomena [do not cease] for them...
Indeterminate states do not cease. Or, for whom indeterminate states do not cease, do unwholesome states not cease for them?
In the formless realm, at the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, for those [beings] indeterminate states do not cease, but unwholesome states do not [not cease] for them.

Indeterminate states do not cease, and unwholesome states do not cease for all those being reborn, for those in the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those in the immaterial plane at the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states.
9.2.2.1.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where wholesome states do not cease, there unwholesome states do not cease? Yes.
Or, where unwholesome states do not cease, there wholesome states do not cease? Yes.
Where wholesome states do not cease, there indeterminate states do not cease? They do cease.
Or, where indeterminate states do not cease, do wholesome states not cease there? No.
Where unwholesome states do not cease, do indeterminate states not cease there? They do cease.
Or, where indeterminate states do not cease, do unwholesome states not cease there? No.
9.2.2.1.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) In whom and in what [base] do unwholesome states not cease, while wholesome states do not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, in those persons and in that [base], wholesome states do not cease; yet it is not the case that unwholesome states do not cease in them there.

Unwholesome states do not cease. For all those at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those at the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness that is dissociated from both the wholesome and the unwholesome,
and for non-percipient beings— among these, neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states cease.
Or conversely: for whomsoever unwholesome states do not cease at a certain place, do wholesome states not cease there for them as well?
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, unwholesome states do not cease for them there, yet wholesome states do not fail to cease for them there.
[This is also the case] for all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome and dissociated from the wholesome.
At the moment of dissolution, for non-percipient beings, neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states cease there.
For whomsoever wholesome states do not cease in a certain place, do indeterminate states also not cease for them in that same place?
For all those passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome during the course of existence, wholesome states do not cease therein;
yet it is not that indeterminate states do not cease therein for them.

For all those being reborn, and at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of dissolution of unwholesome consciousness in the formless realm... [for them...]
In that case, wholesome states do not cease, and indeterminate states also do not cease.
Or rather: for whomsoever, wherever indeterminate states do not cease, for that person there, do wholesome states not cease?

In the formless realm, at the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, for those [beings] there, indeterminate states do not cease; yet it is not the case that for those [beings] wholesome states do not cease.
Therein, wholesome states do not cease. For all those being reborn, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence,
and for those in the formless realm at the ceasing phase of unwholesome states, neither indeterminate states nor wholesome states cease therein.
For whom, where unwholesome states do not cease, for them there, indeterminate states do not cease?

For all those passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome during the course of existence—for these, unwholesome states do not cease there, but it is not that indeterminate states do not cease for them there. For all...

For those beings at the moment of rebirth-linking, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the immaterial plane at the dissolution phase of wholesome states, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states cease therein. Or conversely:
for whomsoever indeterminate states do not cease in a certain place, do unwholesome states also not cease therein for them?
At the moment of the cessation of unwholesome states in the immaterial realm, indeterminate states do not cease for them there;

yet it is not that unwholesome states do not cease for them there. For all those being reborn, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and at the moment of the cessation of wholesome states in the immaterial realm, neither do indeterminate states cease for them there.
And unwholesome states do not cease.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala)
For whomsoever wholesome states have ceased, for that person unwholesome states have ceased? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever unwholesome states have ceased, for that person wholesome states have ceased? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states have ceased, for that person indeterminate states have ceased? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states have ceased, have wholesome states ceased for them? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states have ceased, have indeterminate states ceased for them? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states have ceased, have unwholesome states ceased for them? Yes.
9.2.2.2.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where wholesome states have ceased, have unwholesome states ceased there? Yes.
Or else, where unwholesome states have ceased, have wholesome states ceased there? Yes.
Wherever wholesome states have ceased, have indeterminate states ceased there? Yes.
Or, wherever indeterminate states have ceased, have wholesome states ceased there?
In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states have ceased there, but wholesome states have not ceased there.
In the fourfold plane and the fivefold plane, there have ceased therein both indeterminate states and wholesome states.
Where unwholesome states have ceased, have indeterminate states ceased there? Yes.
Or, conversely, where indeterminate states have ceased, have unwholesome states ceased there?
In the case of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), indeterminate (*abyākata*) phenomena have ceased there, but unwholesome (*akusala*) phenomena have not ceased there.
In the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes, both indeterminate phenomena and unwholesome phenomena have ceased there.
9.2.2.2.3. Positive Correlation: Person and Plane (*Anulomapuggalokāsa*)
For whomsoever wholesome states have ceased at a certain place, for that person have unwholesome states ceased at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states have ceased at a certain place, for that person have wholesome states ceased at that same place?
For those in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) when a second unwholesome consciousness is occurring, unwholesome states have ceased for them at that place, but wholesome states have not.
And for them, wholesome states did not cease there. For others—those belonging to the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes—both unwholesome states and wholesome states ceased there.
For whomsoever wholesome states ceased there, did indeterminate states also cease there? Yes.
Or conversely: for whomsoever indeterminate states had ceased at a certain place, had wholesome states also ceased for them at that same place?

For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), indeterminate states had ceased there, but wholesome states had not ceased for them there. For others, however, among those belonging to the fourfold aggregate (catuvokāra)...
For those belonging to the five-aggregate realm, both indeterminate states and wholesome states have ceased there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states have ceased in a certain place, have indeterminate states also ceased for them there? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states have ceased in a certain place, have unwholesome states also ceased for them there?
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, for those non-percipient beings,

indeterminate states have ceased there, but unwholesome states have not ceased there. For others— those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes— both indeterminate states and unwholesome states have ceased there.
9.2.2.2.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states had not ceased, for that person had unwholesome states not ceased? None.
Or else, for whom unwholesome states had not ceased, for that person had wholesome states not ceased? None.
For whom wholesome states did not cease, for them indeterminate states did not cease? None.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states did not cease, for them wholesome states did not cease? None.
For whom unwholesome states did not cease, for them indeterminate states did not cease? None.
Or again, for whom indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) have not ceased, have unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*) not ceased for them? None.
9.2.2.2.5. Negative Spatial Analysis:
Where wholesome states have not ceased, have unwholesome states not ceased there? Yes.
Or, where unwholesome states have not ceased, have wholesome states not ceased there? Yes.
Where wholesome states have not ceased, have indeterminate states not ceased there? They have ceased.
Or, where indeterminate states have not ceased, have wholesome states not ceased there? There is none.
Where unwholesome states did not cease, did indeterminate states not cease there? They did cease.
Or else, where indeterminate states did not cease, did unwholesome states not cease there? There is none.
9.2.2.2.6. Negative Person-Plane Analysis.
For whomsoever wholesome states have not ceased at a certain place, have unwholesome states not ceased for them at that same place?

For those in the second unwholesome consciousness of the Pure Abodes, wholesome states have not ceased there, but it is not the case that unwholesome states have not ceased for them there. [This is so] when the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring.
In the case of non-percipient beings, neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states have ceased there.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states have not ceased in a certain place, have wholesome states also not ceased for them there? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states have not ceased in a certain place, have indeterminate states also not ceased for them there?
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) is occurring, for those non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), wholesome states (kusaladhamma) have not ceased there,
but indeterminate states (abyākatadhamma) have not failed to cease there either. For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes,
neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states have ceased there.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate (abyākata) states had not ceased at a certain place, had wholesome (kusala) states not also ceased for them there? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome (akusala) states had not ceased at a certain place, had indeterminate states not also ceased for them there?
[They have not] for the Pure Abode (suddhāvāsa) beings when their second consciousness is occurring, and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta); for these, unwholesome states had not ceased there.

[It was] ceased for them, but indeterminate states were not ceased for them there. For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states were ceased there.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states were not ceased there, were unwholesome states not ceased for them there? Yes.
9.2.2.3. The Section on the Future (Anāgatavāra) 9.2.2.3.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom wholesome states will cease, for that person will unwholesome states cease?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness,
wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) will cease, but unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) will not cease for them.
For others, both wholesome states and unwholesome states will cease.
Or rather, for whom unwholesome states will cease, for that person will wholesome states cease? Yes.
For whom wholesome states will cease, for that person will indeterminate states cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will cease, for that person will wholesome states cease?
At the moment of the cessation of the highest path, for those who are Arahants, indeterminate states will cease,
but wholesome states will not cease for them. For others, both indeterminate states and wholesome states will cease.
For whom unwholesome states will cease, for them indeterminate states will cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will cease, for them unwholesome states will cease?
[They will not cease] for those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) and for Arahants; nor for one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the highest path.
For those [beings], indeterminate states will cease, but unwholesome states will not cease for them.
For others, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states will cease.
9.2.2.3.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states will cease, will unwholesome states cease there?
… [as before] … 9.2.2.3.3. Positive Person-Space:
In whomsoever wholesome states will cease at a particular place, will unwholesome states cease for that person at that place?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness,
wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) will cease therein, but unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) will not cease therein. For others— namely,
those belonging to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms— both wholesome and unwholesome states will cease therein.
And unwholesome states will cease. Or rather:
for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease at a certain place, will wholesome states also cease for that person at that same place? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states will cease at a certain place, will indeterminate states also cease for that person at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely: for whomsoever, wherever, indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will cease, will wholesome states (kusala-dhamma) also cease there for them?

At the moment of dissolution of the supreme path (agga-magga), and for Arahants and non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), indeterminate states will cease there, but wholesome states will not cease there for them.
For others, those belonging to the four-constituent (catuvokāra) realm...
For those belonging to the five-aggregate realm, both indeterminate states and wholesome states will cease there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states will cease in a certain place, will indeterminate states also cease for them there? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease in a certain place, will unwholesome states also cease for them there? [No.]

For those possessing the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following will attain the supreme path—as well as for non-percipient beings—indeterminate (abyākata) phenomena will cease there; yet unwholesome (akusala) phenomena will not cease there for them.
For others, namely those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes, indeterminate phenomena...
...and unwholesome states will cease.
9.2.2.3.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala):
For whom wholesome states will not cease, for that person will unwholesome states not cease? Yes.
Or, for whom unwholesome states will not cease, will wholesome states not cease for them?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, unwholesome states will not cease, but it is not the case that wholesome states will not cease for them. At the moment of the supreme path...
At the moment of the dissolution [of the path] of Arahants, neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states will cease for them.
For one in whom wholesome states will not cease, will indeterminate states not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (agga-magga) of Arahants, wholesome states will not cease for them, but [indeterminate states will cease].
For those [beings], indeterminate states will not cease. At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, for them neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states will cease.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease, for that person will wholesome states not cease? Yes.
For whom unwholesome states will not cease, for them indeterminate states will not cease?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those who will attain the highest path immediately after this consciousness, unwholesome states will not cease;
yet for them, it is not the case that indeterminate states will not cease.
At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, neither unwholesome states nor indeterminate states will cease for those [beings].
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease, will unwholesome states also not cease for them? Yes.
9.2.2.3.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa) Where wholesome states will not cease, will unwholesome states not cease there? … [as before] … 9.2.2.3.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whomsoever wholesome states will not cease at a certain place, for that person unwholesome states will not cease at that place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states will not cease at a certain place, for that person wholesome states will not cease at that place?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for those whose consciousness immediately following it will attain the supreme path—for them [it is so].
In that case, unwholesome states will not cease, but wholesome states do not necessarily not cease there for them.
At the moment of the destruction of the supreme path, and for Arahants and non-percipient beings,
neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states will cease there.
For whomsoever wholesome states will not cease at a certain place, for that person at that place will indeterminate states not cease?

At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (agga-magga), and for Arahants and non-percipient beings—at these persons, at those places, wholesome states will not cease, but it is not the case that indeterminate states will not cease for them at those places. [This applies to] the final consciousness...
At the moment of dissolution, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states will cease therein for those [beings].
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease in a certain place, will wholesome states also not cease therein for that person? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states will not cease in a certain place, will indeterminate states also not cease therein for that person?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the highest path,
and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta)— in these cases, unwholesome states (akusala-dhamma) will not cease there,
but indeterminate states (abyākata-dhamma) will not fail to cease there either. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness (pacchimacitta), for them, unwholesome states...
[It is] that indeterminate states will not cease and indeterminate states will not cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever and wherever indeterminate states will not cease, for that person there, will unwholesome states not cease? Yes.
9.2.2.4. Section on the Present and the Past.
9.2.2.4.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom wholesome states cease, for that person have unwholesome states ceased? Yes.
Or rather, for whom unwholesome states have ceased, for that person do wholesome states cease?
In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, unwholesome states have ceased, but wholesome states do not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, both unwholesome states and wholesome states cease for them.
For whom wholesome states cease, for that person have indeterminate states ceased? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom indeterminate states have ceased, for that person do wholesome states cease?

[This is not so] for all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for those who have attained cessation.
In the case of non-percipient beings, indeterminate states have ceased, but wholesome states do not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, both indeterminate states and wholesome states have ceased for them.
For whomsoever unwholesome states cease, for that person have indeterminate states ceased? Yes.
Or, for whom indeterminate states have ceased, do unwholesome states cease for them?
For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome at the moment of its dissolution,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— indeterminate states have ceased for them, but unwholesome states do not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, indeterminate states have ceased and unwholesome states are ceasing for those [beings].
9.2.2.4.2. Positive Plane:
Where wholesome states cease, have unwholesome states ceased there? …pe….
9.2.2.4.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what [sphere], do wholesome states cease?
In that same person, and in that same sphere, had unwholesome states ceased? Yes.
Or conversely, in whom, and in what [sphere], had unwholesome states ceased? In that same person, and in that same sphere, do wholesome states cease? Yes.
In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and in those with a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution,
unwholesome states have ceased there, but wholesome states do not cease there.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, both unwholesome states and wholesome states have ceased there.
For whom, where wholesome states cease, for that person there have indeterminate states ceased? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom, where indeterminate states have ceased, for that person there wholesome states cease?
[This is so] for all at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for non-percipient beings.
In those [beings], indeterminate states have ceased there, but wholesome states do not cease there.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, both indeterminate states and wholesome states have ceased there.
For one in whom unwholesome states cease at a certain place, have indeterminate states ceased there? Yes.
Or alternatively: for whomsoever, wherever, indeterminate states (*abyākata-dhamma*) have ceased, do unwholesome states (*akusala-dhamma*) cease for them there?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for non-percipient beings—at these, indeterminate states have ceased, but unwholesome states do not cease for them there.
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, indeterminate states have ceased and unwholesome states are ceasing for those persons at that place.
9.2.2.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states do not cease, for that person have unwholesome states not ceased? They have ceased.
Or, for whom unwholesome states did not cease, for that person do wholesome states not cease? None.
For whom wholesome states do not cease, for that person did indeterminate states not cease? They did cease.
Or, for whom indeterminate states did not cease, for that person do wholesome states not cease? None.
For whom unwholesome states do not cease, for that person have indeterminate states not ceased? They have ceased.
Or else, for whom indeterminate states have not ceased, for that person do unwholesome states not cease? There is none.
9.2.2.4.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where wholesome states do not cease, have unwholesome states not ceased there? … [as before] … 9.2.2.4.6.
Negative Person-Space:
For whom, where wholesome states do not cease, have unwholesome states not ceased there for them?
In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and in those with a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution, wholesome states do not cease there;
yet unwholesome states have not failed to cease there for them.
Also, when the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, wholesome states do not cease there for them.
Unwholesome states do not cease, nor have they ceased. Or rather:
for whomsoever unwholesome states have not ceased at a certain place, do wholesome states not cease for that person at that place? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states do not cease at a certain place, have indeterminate states not ceased for that person at that place?

In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, in those with unwholesome-dissociated consciousness at the moment of its cessation, and in non-percipient beings—wholesome states do not cease therein;
yet indeterminate states have not failed to cease therein for them.
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes, wholesome states do not cease therein.
And indeterminate states have not ceased.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states have not ceased at a certain place, do wholesome states not cease for that person at that place? Yes.
For whomsoever unwholesome states do not cease at a certain place, have indeterminate states not ceased for that person at that place?

In all those at the moment of arising of consciousness, in those at the moment of dissolution of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, and in non-percipient beings, unwholesome states do not cease there;
yet indeterminate states have not failed to cease there for them.
For those reborn in the Pure Abodes, unwholesome states do not cease there, and [indeterminate states] also do not cease there for them.
And indeterminate states have not ceased.
Or rather, for whomsoever and wherever indeterminate states have not ceased, do unwholesome states not cease for that person there? Yes.
9.2.2.5. Chapter on the Present and Future.
9.2.2.5.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom wholesome states cease, for that person will unwholesome states cease?

At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path—for such a person [unwholesome states will cease].
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, wholesome states cease for them, but unwholesome states will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of other wholesome states, both wholesome states cease and unwholesome states will cease for them.
Or, for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease, do wholesome states cease for them?
For all those at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness dissociated from the wholesome,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— unwholesome states will cease for them, but wholesome states do not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, unwholesome states will cease and wholesome states also cease for those [persons].
For one in whom wholesome states cease, will indeterminate states cease for him? Yes.
Or rather, for one in whom indeterminate states will cease, do wholesome states cease for him? Yes.
In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, in those with a consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution,
and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease, but wholesome states do not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, both indeterminate and wholesome states cease for them.
For whom unwholesome states cease, for them indeterminate states will cease? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom indeterminate states will cease, for them unwholesome states cease?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease, but unwholesome states do not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states will cease for them.
9.2.2.5.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherever wholesome states cease, will unwholesome states cease there?
… [as before] … 9.2.2.5.3. Positive Person-Space:
In whomsoever, wherever, wholesome states cease, will unwholesome states cease for that person there?
At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (aggamagga), and at the moment of the cessation of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path—
wholesome states cease for them there, but unwholesome states will not cease for them there. At the moment of the cessation of other wholesome states, wholesome states cease for them there...
...wholesome states cease and unwholesome states will cease.
Or else, for whomsoever and wherever unwholesome states will cease, do wholesome states cease for them there? [They do not.

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution—at these persons and in this place—[wholesome states do not cease].
Unwholesome states will cease, but wholesome states do not cease for those [persons] there.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, both unwholesome states will cease and wholesome states cease for them there.
For whomsoever wholesome states cease there, will indeterminate states cease for that person there? Yes.
Or again, for whomsoever and wherever indeterminate states (abyākata-dhammā) will cease, do wholesome states (kusala-dhammā) cease for them there?
For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution,
and for non-percipient beings— at these, indeterminate states will cease, but wholesome states do not cease for them there.
At the moment of the dissolution of wholesome states, for those persons, indeterminate states will cease there and wholesome states also cease there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states cease there, for that person will indeterminate states cease there? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease there, for that person do unwholesome states cease there?
In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and in those with unwholesome dissociated consciousness at the moment of its dissolution,
and in non-percipient beings— indeterminate states will cease there, but unwholesome states do not cease there for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of unwholesome states, both indeterminate states and unwholesome states will cease there for them.
9.2.2.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states do not cease, for them unwholesome states will not cease?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, wholesome states do not cease, yet unwholesome states will not fail to cease for them.

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, and for Arahants at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, wholesome states do not cease for them.
And unwholesome states will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever unwholesome states will not cease, do wholesome states not cease for them?
At the moment of the dissolution of the highest path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the highest path—
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, unwholesome states will not cease for them, yet wholesome states do not fail to cease for them.

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, for Arahants, and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, unwholesome states will not cease for them...
Will wholesome states cease, while unwholesome states do not cease?
For one in whom wholesome states do not cease, will indeterminate states not cease? [The answer is:

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, wholesome states do not cease, yet indeterminate states will not fail to cease for them.
At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, for them both wholesome states do not cease and indeterminate states will not cease.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will not cease, do wholesome states not cease for them? Yes.
For whom unwholesome states do not cease, will indeterminate states not cease for them?

[They will not] for all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, unwholesome states do not cease, yet indeterminate states will not fail to cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for those beings, both unwholesome states do not cease and indeterminate states will not cease.
Or again, for whom indeterminate states will not cease, for that person do unwholesome states not cease?
Yes. 9.2.2.5.5. Negative Plane:
Where wholesome states do not cease, there do unwholesome states not cease? ... [and so on] ...
9.2.2.5.6. Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what plane, wholesome states do not cease;
will unwholesome states not cease in that person, in that same plane?
[They do not] in all persons at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and in those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution, in that [plane].
Wholesome states do not cease, yet unwholesome states will not fail to cease for them there.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, for Arahants, for those whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path at the moment of its arising,
and for non-percipient beings— wholesome states do not cease for them there.
And unwholesome states will not cease.
Or, where unwholesome states will not cease for someone, do wholesome states not cease for that person at that place?

At the moment of the dissolution of the highest path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the highest path—[for such a person, wholesome states do not cease].
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, unwholesome states will not cease for them there,
but wholesome states do not fail to cease for them there. At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, in Arahants,
at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, and in non-percipient beings.
In those [beings], unwholesome states will not cease there, and wholesome states do not cease there.
For one in whom wholesome states do not cease at a certain place, will indeterminate states not cease for him at that same place?

[This is so] for all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those with consciousness dissociated from the wholesome at the moment of its dissolution, and for non-percipient beings.
For them, wholesome states do not cease there, yet indeterminate states will not fail to cease for them there.
At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, for them, neither wholesome states nor indeterminate states cease there.
Or rather: For whomsoever, wherever, indeterminate states will not cease, for that person there, do wholesome states not cease? Yes.
For whomsoever, wherever, unwholesome states do not cease, for that person there, will indeterminate states not cease?

[They will not cease] in all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, in the moment of the dissolution of consciousness dissociated from the unwholesome, and in the case of non-percipient beings.
For them, unwholesome states do not cease there, yet indeterminate states will not fail to cease there for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for them, both unwholesome states do not cease there and indeterminate states will not cease there.
Or again, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease at a certain place, do unwholesome states not cease for that person at that place? Yes.
9.2.2.6. Chapter on the Past and Future.
9.2.2.6.1. Positive Person.
For whom wholesome states have ceased, will unwholesome states cease for them?

For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) and for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path—for these, wholesome states have ceased, but unwholesome states will not cease for them. For others...
In those [persons], wholesome states have ceased and unwholesome states will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever unwholesome states will cease, for that person have wholesome states ceased? Yes.
For whomsoever wholesome states have ceased, for that person will indeterminate states cease?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, wholesome states have ceased for those persons, but indeterminate states will not cease for them.
For others, both wholesome states have ceased and indeterminate states will cease.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease, have wholesome states ceased for them? Yes.
For whom unwholesome states have ceased, will indeterminate states cease for them?
At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, unwholesome states have ceased for them, but indeterminate states will not cease for them.
For others, both unwholesome states have ceased and indeterminate states [will cease].
Indeterminate states will cease for that person. Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease, have unwholesome states ceased for them? Yes.
9.2.2.6.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa).
Wherever wholesome states have ceased, will unwholesome states cease there? … [etc.
… 9.2.2.6.3. Positive Person-Space:
In whomsoever, wherever, wholesome states have ceased, will unwholesome states cease for that person there?

For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) and for Arahants, as well as for those whose consciousness immediately following will attain the highest path, wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) have ceased there;
yet unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) will not cease there for them.
For others—those belonging to the four-constituent (catuvokāra) and five-constituent (pañcavokāra) realms—both wholesome states and [unwholesome states] have ceased there.
And unwholesome states will cease.
Or, in whomsoever unwholesome states will cease at a certain place, have wholesome states ceased for them at that same place?
For those in the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes, unwholesome states will cease there.

And for those [beings], wholesome states had not ceased there. For others—those belonging to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—both unwholesome states will cease there and wholesome states had ceased there.
For one in whom wholesome states had ceased there, will indeterminate states cease there?
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, wholesome states have ceased for them there,
but indeterminate states will not cease for them there. For others— those of the four-constituent and five-constituent planes—
both wholesome states have ceased and indeterminate states will cease there.
Or alternatively, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease at a certain place, have wholesome states ceased for them there?

For those in the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa) and for non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease there, but wholesome states have not ceased for them there. For others belonging to the four-constituent [beings]...
For those of the five-aggregate realm, indeterminate states will cease there and wholesome states have ceased there.
For whomsoever unwholesome states have ceased there, will indeterminate states cease there for them?
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, unwholesome states have ceased for them there, but indeterminate states do not [cease] for them there.

In that case, indeterminate states will cease. For those others belonging to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate planes, both unwholesome states have ceased and indeterminate states will cease there.
Or, for whomsoever indeterminate states will cease in a certain plane, have unwholesome states ceased for them there as well?
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, for those non-percipient beings, indeterminate states will cease there,

but unwholesome states have not ceased there for them. For others— those with four aggregates and those with five aggregates— both indeterminate states will cease there and unwholesome states have ceased there.
9.2.2.6.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom wholesome states have not ceased, for that person will unwholesome states not cease? There is none.
Or else, for whom unwholesome states will not cease, for that person have wholesome states not ceased? They have ceased.
For whom wholesome states (*kusalā dhammā*) have not ceased, for them indeterminate states (*abyākatā dhammā*) will not cease? None.
Or rather, for whom indeterminate states will not cease, for them wholesome states have not ceased? They have ceased.
For whom unwholesome states (*akusalā dhammā*) have not ceased, for them indeterminate states will not cease? None.
Or else, for whom indeterminate states will not cease, have unwholesome states not ceased for them? They have ceased.
9.2.2.6.5. Negative Plane:
Where wholesome states have not ceased, will unwholesome states not cease there? ... [and so on] ...
9.2.2.6.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) In whom, where, wholesome states have not ceased, will unwholesome states not cease there for them?
For those in the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), wholesome states have not ceased there.
And yet, unwholesome states will not cease for them there. For those non-percipient beings, neither wholesome states nor unwholesome states have ceased there.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever unwholesome states will not cease there, have wholesome states ceased for them there?

For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) and for Arahants, as well as for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path, unwholesome states (akusalā dhammā) will not cease there;
yet it is not that wholesome states (kusalā dhammā) have not ceased there for them.
For non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), neither unwholesome states nor wholesome states will cease there.

And [it is such that] wholesome states did not cease for him. For whomsoever wholesome states did not cease at a certain place, will indeterminate states not cease for him at that same place? They will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever indeterminate states will not cease at a certain place, did wholesome states not cease for him at that same place? They did cease.
For whom, where unwholesome states have not ceased, will indeterminate states not cease there? They will cease.
Or rather, for whom, where indeterminate states will not cease, have unwholesome states not ceased there? They have ceased.
The Chapter on Cessation.
